bibliographic.title: Generative AI and large language models in health care: pathways to implementation
bibliographic.citation_apa: Generative AI and large language models in health care: pathways to implementation. (2024). npj Digital Medicine, 7, 62. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-023-00988-4

methodology.study_design: editorial perspective synthesizing prior review literature and proposing an evaluation checklist
methodology.sample_description: No primary sample; references Wornow et al. review of 84 foundation models trained on clinical structured text data from EMRs
methodology.technology_context: generative AI and LLMs applied to electronic medical records, EHR integrations, clinical language models, EMR representation models, chatbots, and clinical digital assistants

eligibility.decision_rationale: The document is a healthcare editorial on generative AI and LLMs with conversational interfaces and regulated-context concerns such as privacy and FDA responsibility, but its primary contribution is an EMR model evaluation checklist and implementation pathways rather than conversational governance mechanisms such as oversight, audit, guardrails, or contestability.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Provided text is partial, author names are not visible, and governance content may appear in unread sections.

appraisal.notes: Editorial synthesis without primary empirical methods; useful for implementation framing and regulated healthcare context but weak as standalone methodological evidence for conversational governance.

cerqual.explanation: The text coherently links LLM healthcare applications to implementation and evaluation concerns, but offers limited direct evidence on conversational governance controls; confidence is moderate because the excerpt is incomplete and the piece is opinion/editorial rather than empirically grounded.

coding.theme: Implementation and evaluation of generative AI and LLMs in healthcare EMRs
coding.subtheme: Conversational tools and clinical digital assistants in regulated health systems
rq_alignment: partial alignment with governance via privacy, regulation, and evaluation criteria

synthesis.main_claim: The editorial argues that health systems need structured pathways and an evaluation checklist to implement generative AI and LLM models on electronic medical records, building on a large prior review of clinical foundation models.
synthesis.contribution: Provides contextual implementation framing for healthcare LLMs, references an EMR-focused model taxonomy, and highlights regulated deployment examples including EHR-integrated conversational tools.
synthesis.limitations: No primary empirical study design; conversational governance is not the central focus; provided text is truncated and authorship is unclear.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting contextual evidence on healthcare LLM implementation, EMR evaluation criteria, privacy and regulatory responsibility, and examples of conversational clinical assistants rather than as central evidence on conversational governance architecture.
